keys.title: Keys
keys.mod.browser: On macOS the main modifier is Cmd — in the browser too. Out of a hundred-odd Cmd shortcuts Chrome keeps five: new tab, close tab, new window, quit, and find-selection. Everything else reaches the page and we take it. Elsewhere the main modifier is Control.
keys.mod.electron: In the desktop app the main modifier is Cmd on macOS and Control elsewhere. Nothing else claims it there.
keys.clip: Copy and paste stay on the system key — Cmd on macOS, Control elsewhere. That habit comes from the system, not from this file.
keys.captured: While this window is open, keys are shown but not run — nothing behind it moves. Escape is caught too, so close with the × in the corner.
keys.echo.none: press any shortcut — it will show up here
keys.echo.hint: Nothing shows up at all? The system or the browser took the key before us — Cmd+T, Cmd+W, Cmd+N, Cmd+Q and Cmd+E never reach the page, and on macOS Control+arrows belong to Spaces. Shows up as a different key? Then your modifiers are remapped.
keys.elsewhere: You are looking at the other layout. Both live in the same keymap.json — this one just is not the one running now.
keys.taken: Not ours — {count} shortcuts the system or the browser keeps (a couple we left it on purpose)
keys.soft: Taken back from the browser — {count} shortcuts that would otherwise be its own
